units.text: The 2001 USGS state elevation table lists Mount Elbert at 14,433 feet, not 14,494 feet.

judgement.reason: The passage shows the table lists Mount Elbert at 14,433 feet, which directly contradicts the alternative 14,494 feet.

units.text: The 14,494-foot figure originates from the 1967 summit over-14,000 feet table, not the 2001 table.

judgement.reason: The passage does not mention 14,494 feet, the 1967 table, or the 2001 table, only Mount Elbert's 14,433-foot elevation.

units.text: USGS elevation updates from 2002 changed Mount Elbert's official height to 14,440 feet, replacing the prior 14,433-foot measurement.

citations.title: How Tall is Mt Elbert? Unraveling the Height of Colorado's Greatest 14er | The Next Summit: A Mountain Blog

judgement.reason: The passages state that Mt. Elbert was officially 14,433 feet until 2002, when USGS updated maps showed it was 7 feet taller, making the official elevation 14,440 feet.
